page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the Tau T2D machine family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, resulting in 4 vCPUs. It is equipped with 16 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. This configuration does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing it in the top 25% of its class. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and Passmark CPU metrics generally align with the middle 50% average. Memory bandwidth is stable, recording 48.77 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 34.91 GB/sec for write operations. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput represent relative performance bottlenecks, falling into the bottom 25% tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2d-standard-4 offers dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, which provides predictable compute performance per resource unit for non-shared workloads. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, software compilation, database operations, and lightweight LLM inference tasks. The lack of local storage and GPU acceleration makes it less suitable for heavy storage-bound databases or deep learning training.
